question: How many digital Kisan Credit Cards had been created in India by March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**7.75 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• By March 2025, a total of **7.75 crore digital Kisan Credit Cards (KCC)** had been created in India to support farmers.
 
• The KCC scheme was introduced in 1998 by the Government of India in collaboration with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and NABARD to provide farmers with timely access to credit.
 
• The **digitalization of the Kisan Credit Card** has enabled easier access to credit and streamlined processes, reducing paperwork and time.
 
• The KCC initiative has been pivotal in providing **short-term credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses, and working capital** for allied agricultural activities.
 
• The government has been actively promoting the issuance of KCCs to small and marginal farmers, with a focus on ensuring financial inclusion in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme**

 
 
• Launched in 1998, the scheme aims to provide **adequate and timely credit support** to farmers for agricultural needs.
 
• It includes provisions for crop loans, working capital for farm maintenance, and allied activities like dairy and fisheries.
 
• Farmers can avail loans at subsidized interest rates under the scheme, with interest subventions provided by the government.
 
• The digital version of KCC ensures faster loan disbursement and real-time tracking of transactions.
 
 
 
• **Role of NABARD and RBI**
 
 
• The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) play key roles in implementing and monitoring the KCC scheme.
 
• NABARD provides guidelines to banks for issuing KCCs and ensures that the credit needs of farmers are met.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion through KCC**
 
 
• Digital KCCs have significantly contributed to financial inclusion, particularly in rural India.
 
• They empower farmers by providing access to institutional credit, reducing dependence on informal sources like moneylenders.
 
 
 
• **Other Farmer-Centric Initiatives**
 
 
• **PM Kisan Samman Nidhi:** Provides direct income support of ₹6,000 annually to farmers.
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme:** Provides farmers with information on soil nutrient status to improve crop productivity.
 
• **Fasal Bima Yojana:** Ensures crop insurance against natural calamities.
